A standalone checker establishes symbolic identities and independent exact finite Markov computations; no finite sampling is substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The chosen object is the smallest connected two-group hypergraph with overlapping three-person social interactions; this gives a motivated precise test of how strong group unanimity preference delays global consensus. The sharp (5/2)2^q delay and a complete rational time law quantify metastability in a finite fixed structure, while the 3/4-agent uniform-boundedness theorem makes the five-person cutoff structural rather than an arbitrary small computation. This establishes an interpretable boundary between mean-field intuition and polarized network trapping without claiming a universal law.
